slides.title: Learn by acting, observing consequences, and revising a policy

segments.label: Concept and boundary
segments.text: Reinforcement learning replaces a known transition model with experience. An agent acts, observes consequences, receives reward, and revises a policy or value estimate. The recurring loop is interaction, return, value, and control, with uncertainty made visible rather than erased.

slides.title: Reinforcement learning seeks high expected return; optimality is not automatic

segments.label: Concept and boundary
segments.text: Reinforcement learning seeks high expected return, but successful learning is not automatic. Sparse feedback, partial observability, unsafe exploration, unstable approximation, and distribution shift can all break the promise. Separate the objective from the evidence that an algorithm actually reaches it.

slides.title: The source contrasts batch learning with incremental online learning

segments.label: Concept and boundary
segments.text: Batch and online learning describe update schedules. Batch learning updates after collecting a dataset; online learning updates as examples arrive. Reinforcement learning is instead defined by sequential decisions and reward, so it may use either batch or online updates.

slides.title: A policy chooses; value functions predict long-run consequences

segments.label: Concept and boundary
segments.text: A policy chooses actions; state and action values predict expected long-run return. Q learning will store action values because control requires comparing choices at the same state. ACTION VALUE Q pi (s,a)=E pi [Gₜ|sₜ=s,aₜ=a] Expected return after taking action a, then following pi . How good is this choice here?
